entries.title: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill Calls for Her Lieutenant Governor to Resign
entries.summary: An ethics investigation found Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell harassed a staffer and violated ethics rules.
entries.content:
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill called for the resignation of her second in command, Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell, after ethics investigators concluded his behavior constituted sexual harassment and violated ethics standards.

A 61-page report by investigators for an outside law firm includes evidence that Caldwell sought a promotion for his girlfriend, brought guests to ticketed events without payment and told a female staff member that young women want "young sperm.”

Sherrill announced the findings Thursday on X and gave Caldwell “until tomorrow” to resign. The two were elected on the same ticket and took office in January.

“The Lieutenant Governor’s resignation is necessary and in the best interest of New Jersey residents,” she said. “The investigation found that the Lieutenant Governor engaged in serious, repeated violations of state policy and failed to uphold the responsibilities of his office.”

The report followed an anonymous complaint received by the governor’s chief ethics officer in May. Investigators with the law firm Lowenstein Sandler found Caldwell, 66, made the sexual remark after a staffer told him a friend was not interested in a relationship with the lieutenant governor.

Caldwell then remarked that the staffer and her friend “needed a man who was in a position to help them,” the report states, before going on to make additional crude statements.

The unnamed staffer told investigators the incident was “textbook sexual harassment" and caused her take measures to distance herself from Caldwell at work and to avoid traveling with him.

Caldwell denied making the comment, the report said, but investigators found his account lacked credibility given numerous similar incidents and contemporaneous documentation provided by the staffer.

Sherrill said the ethics violations persisted despite “multiple warnings and trainings.”

“The substantiated finding of sexual harassment is extremely troubling,” she said. “I’ve seen firsthand how a hostile culture can undermine everyone’s ability to succeed. It’s insidious and ruptures the trust within an organization.”

The report also found that Caldwell used his government email to seek a promotion for his girlfriend, who is a state employee, four days after receiving notice of the ethics investigation. He did not disclose their relationship in the communications, and the woman did not receive a promotion, raise or other benefits.

Investigators also found Caldwell routinely brought guests to ticketed events without payment, despite receiving guidance from ethics officials.

Caldwell did not immediately respond to The Washington Sun’s request for comment.

entries.title: Trump and Xi Toast to Mutual Cooperation at Opulent White House State Dinner
entries.summary: The guest list included more than 130 people, including tech executives and three Supreme Court justices.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping for a lavish White House state dinner Thursday night, pairing Chinese emissaries with American billionaires and government officials against the backdrop of ongoing trade and technology negotiations.

Dignitaries gathered in the East Room — which was draped in red linens and decorated with blossoms, dahlias, ranunculus and gold-plated silver — and heard the two state leaders’ toasts over glasses of Schramsberg “Blanc De Noir,” the same wine served during President Richard Nixon’s famous 1972 “Toast to Peace” in Beijing.

In his opening address, Trump called Xi and his delegation “truly amazing, outstanding people,” invited the group to tour the unfinished White House ballroom, and gifted Xi with a statue of a bald eagle that he said he designed himself along with first lady Melania Trump.

“As the leaders of our two nations,” Trump said, “President Xi and I both understand that we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we've never gotten along better.”

In his statements, the Chinese president broadly detailed the progress made since Trump’s visit to China in May, when the two leaders agreed to further bilateral ties. Xi and Trump had “sincere and in-depth exchanges,” the state leader said, and had reached “common understanding on many issues.”

“This has added new substance to the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability,” Xi said, adding that “China and the United States must act as responsible major countries, meet the expectations of our peoples, keep pace with the trend of our times, and explore a new approach for major countries to get along with each other.”

Xi concluded his statements with a toast, lifting his glass to “the friendship of our two peoples.”

APTOPIX Trump Xi (1024x682, AR: 1.50)
The lengthy guest list included more than 130 people, bringing together executives with competing visions for AI governance — a running motif of this week’s summit — including OpenAI’s Sam Altman, who recently urged more international safeguards, and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, who reportedly lobbied Trump against national regulations.

Elon Musk was also listed as a guest, signaling a potential reconciliation after he and Trump had a public falling-out in June 2025. Earlier this month, Trump told Fox News he would not impede Chinese automakers who seek to build electric vehicles in the U.S. — a move that could encroach on Musk’s territory, as Tesla battles Chinese company BYD to lead the world in EV sales and production.

Trump Xi (1024x682, AR: 1.50)
Most reporters were not welcomed into the East Room for the meal, with the exception of a group of Fox News personalities, including Laura Ingraham, Bret Baier and Jesse Watters.

Chief Justice John Roberts and Trump-appointed justices Amy Coney Barrett and Brett Kavanaugh were also invited.

Trump Xi (1024x682, AR: 1.50)
Ahead of Xi’s entrance, a few moments of disorder took place. Outside the executive residence, White House staff turned away reporters from MS NOW and CNN from the arrival ceremony, as reporters were required to get preapproval by Wednesday night to cover the event. At the time, Trump’s ban on the outlets had not yet been lifted.

Protesters waiting for the Chinese motorcade chanted “free Hong Kong” and called for China to release political prisoners ahead of the dinner.

“CCP, your empire will fall! CCP, you’re not welcome!” some shouted.

Just after 7 p.m., Trump and the first lady greeted their Chinese counterparts and stood for photos in the newly renovated North Portico.

The two leaders ignored questions from reporters about Taiwan or artificial intelligence as they entered the White House. Trump also declined to answer whether he had asked Xi to free imprisoned Chinese activist Jimmy Lai, who was arrested and sentenced in 2020 for his role in organizing Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement.

entries.title: All-DMV High School Soccer Players of Week 1
entries.summary: This week’s group features a lockdown defender from the Churchill boys and a potent goal scorer from the St. John’s girls.
entries.content:
This story is part of The Washington Sun’s All-DMV coverage. All-DMV is a new collaboration between The Sun, Fox5 DC, NBC4 Washington and WTOP News, aimed at covering the D.C. area’s best high school athletes. You can find past players of the week and more information about All-DMV here.

The first month of the soccer season was a busy one as local contenders jostled for position against division rivals to boost their resumes come playoff time. Here are six September standouts — three boys and three girls — whose performances earned them All-DMV Player of the Week:

Adiah Aahmez, Sophomore, Midfielder, Bowie

Aahmez has looked comfortable in a new role for a Bowie boys’ team that graduated 11 seniors from last year’s squad, six of whom went on to play collegiate soccer. The sophomore center midfielder picked up a goal and two assists as the Bulldogs scored three early victories against Mount Hebron, Bladensburg and Annapolis Area Christian.

Margaret Brault, Senior, Midfielder, St. John’s

Brault was the star of the St. John’s girls’ blowout win over Elizabeth Seton on Tuesday. She scored four goals in the victory, bringing her tally to six goals on the young season. Brault shines on both sides of the ball — the senior also provides tenacious defense for a Cadets team that’s looking to defend its Washington Catholic Athletic Conference crown.

“She’s constantly a threat, constantly looking to help build a play for her team, and one of those people that just has an immediate impact in the game,” St. John’s coach Allison Diaz said.

Tobi Falayi, Senior, Defender, Churchill

Falayi is the anchor of the Churchill boys’ stout defense. An all-state defender a season ago, Falayi’s constant defensive presence helped the Bulldogs to three shutout victories amid a five-game September winning streak. Their most recent victory came Wednesday in shutout fashion against Maryland Class 4A rival Whitman, an impressive result over a Vikings team that made the state finals last season.

Emery Gregory, Senior, Midfielder, Eleanor Roosevelt

Gregory has wasted little time finding her footing offensively for the Eleanor Roosevelt girls. The senior midfielder is already up to five goals and two assists for the Raiders, who scored an early 3-1 rivalry win over Bowie. The defending Prince George’s County champs also scored 5-0 tournament victories over Guilford Park and Bishop McNamara.

Ege Kirgiz, Senior, Forward/Midfielder, Potomac School

The Potomac School boys raced out to a 3-0 start, and Kirgiz was a big reason why. The left-footed senior picked up three goals and two assists for the Panthers, who took down Saint James (MD), St. Christopher’s and Episcopal. Kirgiz’s steady play as both a forward and midfielder gives coach Travis Beauchamp the ability to unleash him all over the field for the Mid-Atlantic Athletic Conference contenders.

Chloe Russ, Senior, Goalkeeper, Walter Johnson

If the Walter Johnson girls want to make a deep playoff run this season in a loaded division stacked with state title contenders, it’ll need strong defensive play. Russ, the Wildcats’ senior goalkeeper, has helped provide that so far — she didn’t let in a goal in her first three starts of the season. First-year coach Ilyes Ouldbrahim’s team picked up division wins in shutout fashion against Whitman and Quince Orchard.
